The capture-recapture stop rule does not match how our lenses sample defects, and it has no cited source. Chapman's estimator (Lincoln-Petersen family, model M0) assumes two independent captures of one closed population, with every defect equally likely to be caught on each occasion. Our lens groups are designed to catch DIFFERENT defect classes (PACKET.md:38-65), and each lens's planted defect belongs to that lens only (PACKET.md:24-25). So a defect's capture probability is near zero for the off-lens group, which is maximal heterogeneity. Briand, El Emam, Freimut and Laitenberger (ISERN-97-22, fetched) say this equal-probability assumption is the one that 'requires most attention'. In their inspection data heterogeneity dominates and M0 underestimates. They recommend model Mh (jackknife) with 4 or more inspectors. Here the overlap m between groups is ~0 by design, so N = (n1+1)(n2+1)/(m+1) - 1 measures how disjoint the lenses are, not how many defects remain. With m=0 and n1=n2=3, N=15 and 'remaining' is 9, so the gate can never close however clean the plan is. If the groups instead re-report the same known items, m is large and N collapses to the count already found. The bead never defines 'two independent lens groups'. In a clean round new findings are 0 by definition, so n1 and n2 are mostly planted defects, whose catchability the conductor controls.
evidence: var/agent-tmp/converge/r3/issues.jsonl:209 (jev-convergence-gate-g57u) acceptance 3; var/agent-tmp/converge/PACKET.md:24-25,38-65; https://edocs.tib.eu/files/e001/254163734.pdf (Briand et al., ISERN-97-22, section 2.2 assumption (c) and section 4 results: 'the heterogeneity effect dominates', 'MLE for Model Mt and M0 underestimates to a great extent', Mh jackknife recommended for 4+ inspectors)
fix: Replace acceptance 3 with a design that matches the sampling. Either (a) two or more independent reviewers PER LENS on the same snapshot (e.g. the worker pane and the background lens agent), with the estimate computed per lens and Mh-jackknife used once there are 4+ reviewers (Briand et al.); or (b) no capture-recapture: stop on the two-zero-new-rounds rule plus every lens catching its planted defects in both clean rounds. In either case, define the reviewer groups and keep planted defects out of the population count (report them separately) before the round in which the rule is applied.

(1) arXiv:1706.04599 (fetched) is Guo, Pleiss, Sun, Weinberger, 'On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks'. It studies post-hoc calibration of single networks and recommends temperature scaling. It does not evaluate ensembles and does not show that 'calibrated ensembles beat single models'. (2) 'Is this test failure flaky' is a forecast: the label is not in the tokens. DP-52 ('which tests to run / will this diff break a test', 7,272 runs / 1,214 failures) is class d, 'none (forecast; V8 deferred)'. Diff-risk/test-failure forecast AUC is .377 (inverted). Nothing labels a failure flaky vs real, so the classifier has no label to learn or be scored on. (4) Clef is ruled out at hook call sites (PRODUCT.md:88: hook budgets near 1.5 s), yet the WHAT puts a Jev+Clef ensemble in a pre-hook. (5) Reporting PASS when any of five reruns passes turns real intermittent failures into PASS. The bar is set after the first week, and the hook is enabled globally before any measurement.

text: Supported. The numbers match the receipt (47/47 vs 7/47; 1.40% vs 14.81%). The NP cut is fit on one half of the 349 negatives and audited on the other: each half (174/175) meets the 149 negatives that alpha .02 / delta .05 needs, matching the D3 math review.

'Active sampling near the cut' cannot give an unbiased P(drop | relevant). The one-sided bound in acceptance 2 (rule of three / Clopper-Pearson: 0/59 gives .0495) holds only for a simple random sample of relevant memories. Sampling near the Jev cut leaves out the relevant memories that Jev scores far below the cut. Those confident wrong drops are exactly what this estimand guards against, so the estimate is biased low and the bound loses its coverage. Our own math review says the same about PPI: 'not protected against convenience/active sampling unless the design weights are included' (jev-b35c.25 MATH REVIEW, D17). Acceptance 1 asks for a sampling frame and seed but no inclusion probabilities. jev-9cqw takes its labels from here and inherits the bias.
